newsitem.title: USA: NFL-ELWAY LEADS BRONCOS TO ANOTHER FOURTH-QUARTER COMEBACK WIN.
newsitem.headline: NFL-ELWAY LEADS BRONCOS TO ANOTHER FOURTH-QUARTER COMEBACK WIN.

text.p: Denver's veteran star quarterback engineered his 35th career fourth-quarter comeback victory as the Broncos edged the Oakland Raiders 22-21 on Monday night.

Elway found a wide open Rod Smith streaking down the field and connected on a 49-yard touchdown strike with 4:14 remaining as the Broncos won their fifth in a row to raise their record to an AFC-best 8-1.
Elway's fourth-quarter heroics trail only Miami's Dan Marino, who has quarterbacked 40 career fourth-quarter comeback wins.
The winning score came 47 seconds after Jeff Hostetler hooked up with Tim Brown for a 42-yard touchdown play that had put Oakland ahead 21-16.
Hostetler threw for two scores and ran for another for the Raiders, who fell to 4-5.
The Broncos led 16-7 after Jason Elam kicked his third field goal of the game, a 28-yarder with 10:08 left in the fourth quarter.
That's when it looked as if Hostetler was going to pull an Elway.
He moved the Raiders 57 yards in less than three minutes and hit Derrick Fenner with a 15-yard TD toss to lift Oakland within 16-14 with 7:20 to go. Hostetler was 4-for-5 for 61 yards on the drive.

The Broncos were then forced to punt and the Raiders took over at their own 46-yard-line. Hostetler needed only two plays to put his team in front, hitting Brown for a 12-yard gain before finding him again for the long touchdown when defensive back Ray Crockett slipped and left Brown all alone.
Brown finished with eight receptions for 126 yards, while Hostetler was 22-for-34 for 250 yards.
But the Elway magic was too strong for the Raiders to overcome. On 3rd-and-10, Elway froze the Oakland secondary with a pump fake, then found Smith, who scored his first touchdown of the season.
Elway, who also had a 10-yard touchdown toss to Shannon Sharpe in the first quarter, was 16-for-33 for 182 yards.
Denver's Terrell Davis ran for 85 yards on 19 carries to regain the NFL rushing lead with 979 yards. The 36-year-old Elway scampered nine times for 70 yards.
